request.system:
You are given a compliance question and a shortlist of items from a table of contents of investment performance standards (provisions, definitions, interpretive guidance, rulings). Choose the one to three items the question PRIMARILY turns on — the ones a compliance officer would open first.

Rules:
- Pick from the shortlist only, by concept_id. Pick nothing if no item plausibly addresses the question.
- Prefer the provision that states the rule. Add a definition only when the question hinges on what a term means (e.g. whether an account is "discretionary").
- Pick interpretive guidance or a ruling only when the question is specifically about the subject in its title. Do not pick it because it mentions a word in the question.
- Fewer is better. One item is the usual answer; three is the maximum.
request.user:
Question: Must we provide a composite description if a prospect asks?
Topics: composite description availability on request, prospective client requirements

Shortlist:
- prov:composite-description-on-request — Composite description available on request (provision)
- gs:GS-2025-02 — Guidance Statement GS-2025-02 — Composite Minimums (guidance)
- prov:non-fee-paying-inclusion — Inclusion of non-fee-paying portfolios (provision)
- prov:composite-inclusion-timing — Timing of new portfolio inclusion (provision)
- prov:composite-definition-documented — Composite definition documented in writing (provision)
- prov:composite-inclusion-all-discretionary — Inclusion of all fee-paying discretionary portfolios (provision)
- def:benchmark — Benchmark (definition)
- def:significant-cash-flow — Significant cash flow (definition)

entry_concepts.description: concept_ids from the shortlist that the question primarily turns on; empty if none does

response.reason: The question asks directly whether a composite description must be provided when a prospect requests it. The provision 'Composite description available on request' states that rule, so it is the one to open first.
